memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The man asked him, 'What is your name?' 'Jacob,' he answered. Then the man said, 'Your name will no longer be Jacob, but Israel, because you have struggled with God and with humans and have overcome.'" - Gen 32:27-28 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
"What is your name?" the man asks. It is a searching question, because Jacob's name told the truth about him. "Jacob" meant "grasper" or "deceiver" — and he had lived up to it, grabbing his brother's heel at birth and cheating and scheming ever since. To answer "Jacob" was to confess who he had been.

But then comes grace: "Your name will no longer be Jacob, but Israel." God gives him a new name and, with it, a new identity. No longer "the deceiver," but "Israel" — one who has struggled with God and overcome. The grasping cheat is being transformed into a man who wrestles with God in faith and prevails through dependence.

This is one of the great pictures of what God does with a life. He does not merely improve us a little; He gives us a new identity. When we come to Christ, we too receive a new nature: "if anyone is in Christ, the new creation has come: The old has gone, the new is here!" (2 Cor 5:17). Our past labels — failure, deceiver, unwanted, unworthy — no longer define us.

Whatever name your past has given you, hear the good news: God specialises in making new people. He met a grasper named Jacob and left him a man named Israel. He can give you, too, a new name and a new beginning.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What old "name" or label from my past still defines how I see myself?
2. Do I believe God can give me a new identity, not just small improvement?
3. Have I received the new name and new nature God offers in Christ?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You make new people. Take the old names my past has given me, and give me a new identity in You. Transform me, as You transformed Jacob into Israel. Amen.
